chunk_findings.detail: The change widens the DYNAMIC program-call baseline by adding `ddflow.adapters.fs` to the allowed modules for the `DYNAMIC` family. As a result, a dynamic program call implemented in `ddflow/adapters/fs.py` (for example the `shutil.which` lookup mentioned in the new comment) is now accepted by the archifaces guard where it would previously have been rejected. This is a baseline raise for the dynamic family, contrary to the stated rule “Move the sites through their ports; never raise a baseline.” The added regression test is scoped to C6 files by its name and does not inspect this allowlist expansion, so the guard change is not caught by the new test.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces.py:63

chunk_findings.detail: The new test only asserts that the current counted program sites in the listed files are not greater than the existing baseline; it does not verify that the calls are routed through `ddflow.adapters` rather than the `ddflow.infra` compat shims. For example, if `ddflow/services/resultcache.py` is edited back to `from ..infra import git as G` while leaving the same number of counted sites, the test still passes because `n > base.get(...)` is false when the count merely returns to the old baseline value. Thus it cannot fail on the exact regression the change is meant to prevent: a listed file using the compat shim again or replacing one counted site with another while staying at or below baseline.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_c6_git_program_calls.py:test_program_sites_in_c6_files_do_not_exceed_baseline

chunk_findings.detail: The new shim-import absence test only searches for a few exact substrings, so equivalent imports of the forbidden infra shims can bypass it. For example, if `ddflow/services/resultcache.py` is changed to `from ..infra.git import run` (or `from ..infra import (git,)`), none of the listed strings such as `from ..infra import git` or `ddflow.infra.git` appears contiguously, so `back` remains empty and the test passes even though the file still imports the infra git shim. This defeats the added regression guard meant to ensure C6 files route through adapters/ports rather than infra shims.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_c6_git_program_calls.py:test_c6_files_import_the_adapters_not_the_infra_shims

This makes the regression check bypassable by import style.

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test cannot detect growth of JSON-RPC sites in the file it is supposed to guard. By declaring `ddflow.adapters.mcp_wire` as the home, the change causes `I.counts` to omit sites in that module; the test docstring itself says “its sites are not violations.” Consequently, if someone adds another hand-written JSON-RPC site in `ddflow/adapters/mcp_wire.py` (for example, a new `"jsonrpc"` literal or helper), line 15 still passes because the home’s sites are not counted, line 17 still passes, and the worker assertion is unaffected. Thus the promise that the named arch-ratchet test sees no grown site for this family is not kept: growth inside the home is silently allowed. A real guard would need to count the sites in the home explicitly, or move the sites out and assert the exact allowed site set.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_c6_mcp_wire_jsonrpc.py:15
